followups: LiveWorkspacePanel.readContext: the generation guard only changes when the selected run or scope changes. Two reads on the same run can therefore resolve out of order. A late invalid response can set actionError next to a newer validated exactContext, and a late valid response can set exactContext after a newer error. Add a per-read counter, e.g. `const read=++readSeq.current` checked together with the generation, so only the latest read sets context or error. followups.detail: The previous blocker was that two concurrent whole-state saves in one useDesktopState could roll back to an old state while keeping the newer revision, after which the next save passed CAS and erased data. Within one panel instance this is fixed. saveLockRef is checked and set synchronously before mutate() is called. It is released only in a useLayoutEffect keyed on settledCount. setSettledCount is queued after mutate's post-await setState/setRevision calls in the same lane, so the committed render that runs the effect already contains the settled state and revision. Any event that arrives between the settle and the React render hits the held lock and is dropped. No second mutate can capture a stale previous/previousRevision. Every mutating path goes through run(): add/toggle/remove criterion and step, advance, goToEarlierPhase, editSetting, removeSetting, addRule, removeRule, addDecision, togglePin. Because of this, a failure rollback restores the last server-confirmed state, so state and revision stay consistent and a later conflict shows up as a visible 409. Evidence: 01-red on 2de3c4e shows 'Expected: 1, Received: 2' for both race tests. 04-green passes them, including the reload plus further-mutation check and the 500 no-piggyback check.

A→B→A draft clearing is fixed by per-draft version refs that every onChange increments. A draft is cleared only when ok === true and the version is unchanged since submit. Step text and assignee share one version. This is conservative: retyping the same text keeps the draft. 03-red, run on the lock-only intermediate, fails with 'Expected: "Novější koncept", Received: ""'. 04-green passes. scopeRef was removed and nothing depends on it.

The serialization invariant lives in each panel, not in useDesktopState.mutate. mutate still has no in-flight guard. Any other consumer of the hook, or a future caller, that calls mutate concurrently reintroduces the rollback-to-old-state-with-new-revision data loss. AgentPacketPanel and LiveWorkspacePanel were not supplied, so I cannot say whether they call mutate. Recommendation: add a ref-based in-flight guard inside mutate that returns false while a save is pending, and add a hook-level test. This is not blocking for this diff because both of its callers are now serialized.

Pre-existing, now more visible: saveState has no timeout or abort. A POST that never returns (hung server or network) holds saveLockRef forever. 'Znovu načíst' bumps the generation but does not release the lock, which waits for the fetch to settle. The old busy flag got stuck the same way. Now, though, the NodeWorkflowPanel drafts stay editable and Enter is silently ignored. Consider an AbortController or timeout and releasing the lock on reload.

User simulation: pressing Enter in a draft input while a save is pending does nothing. The only cue is the disabled add button, and there is no status or aria-busy. Consider a visible 'Ukládám…' status, or an explicit message when a submit is dropped.

Pre-existing: editSetting saves the whole document on every keystroke, and busy disables the input, so focus is lost after each character. The lock now drops, rather than races, any keystroke that arrives before the disabled render. In practice this window is near zero because discrete events flush synchronously. Consider committing on blur or debouncing.

Pre-existing: drafts are not scoped by project, workspace or node. If project or workspace props change while a save is pending, the lock stays held until the old request settles, which blocks saves on the new scope. The old draft (ok=false) carries over into the new scope. The harness cannot test this because project and workspace come from the query string, not the hash.
